active_themes.label: Talks Over Tankers
active_themes.summary: A brief smoke scare near Riyadh's airport cleared within hours and was not an escalation. Sanctions are tightening anyway: a new Russia sanctions law gives Trump broad tariff powers, and Turkey revoked the license of Iran's Mellat Bank. Fuel prices are still elevated (UK diesel is near £2 a litre), but no Brent crude or Hormuz tanker-traffic print is confirmed, so the oil verdict stays open.

active_themes.label: AI Trade Loses Its Shield
active_themes.summary: Tech leadership has survived the Fed hike. The Nasdaq rose 0.24% today while the Dow fell 0.86%. Higher Q2 growth revisions in the US and UK weaken the 'growth is cracking' argument but also keep rate-cut hopes off the table. A new FTC probe into AI safety adds regulatory risk to the sector the market leans on most.

active_themes.label: The Fix Unwound
active_themes.summary: There is still no confirmed 10-year Treasury yield print. Japan's hike to 1.25% means the world's cheapest borrowed money is tightening alongside the Fed. Indian stocks have now had their longest weekly losing run in 25 years, which fits the pattern of global tightening pressuring emerging markets. Stronger US growth data gives yields less reason to fall.

active_themes.label: Fed Voices Split
active_themes.summary: The Fed's internal watchdog found no criminal wrongdoing in the Powell-era renovation cost overruns. That removes a legal pretext Trump used in his pressure campaign against Powell. There is still no concrete action against Warsh or other officials over the Fed vote. The open question is whether the pressure moves from words to action.

open_watchlist.condition: Brent crude either breaks above $110 or falls back under $100 in the sessions following today's hike.
open_watchlist.meaning: This is the number that decides whether the Fed's next move is a pause or a second hike into a supply shock.

open_watchlist.condition: Any actual shift in Hormuz tanker traffic following Trump's comment that the Iran war is 'towards an end.'
open_watchlist.meaning: Would be the first real evidence that de-escalation talk is translating into lower physical oil-supply risk, not just rhetoric.

open_watchlist.condition: The next 10-year Treasury yield close — whether it lands above 5.25% or drops back under 5%.
open_watchlist.meaning: A drop under 5% confirms today's reported bond rally was real and the inflation-fear premium is genuinely easing; a close above 5.25% says the hike-relief story was a one-day illusion.

open_watchlist.condition: Brent crude's next print relative to the $100 and $110 levels.
open_watchlist.meaning: A break under $100 would be the first hard confirmation behind Trump's Iran de-escalation comments; a push toward $110 says the oil-driven inflation story is still very much alive.

open_watchlist.condition: Whether Trump's comments about the Fed vote move from claims of influence to concrete action against Warsh or other officials.
open_watchlist.meaning: Concrete action, not just rhetoric, is what would turn today's shrugged-off independence story into a real market risk.

open_watchlist.condition: Whether the yen strengthens sharply or the Nikkei sells off in the sessions following the BOJ's hike to 1.25%.
open_watchlist.meaning: The classic signature of a carry-trade unwind that could spill into the same leveraged US tech trade leading this market.

open_watchlist.condition: A session where the Nasdaq falls more than 1% while the Dow holds flat or rises.
open_watchlist.meaning: Leadership has rotated away from tech, which would remove the prop that has been holding the S&P 500 up.

open_watchlist.condition: Indian benchmark stocks extend their losing run into another week.
open_watchlist.meaning: Global tightening is spreading stress into emerging markets, a warning for any investor holding them.

open_watchlist.condition: UK diesel closes above £2 a litre for the first time.
open_watchlist.meaning: Energy costs are feeding through to household budgets, which keeps central banks wary of easing.

open_watchlist.condition: The FTC's AI safety probe produces formal demands or a named target among the large AI companies.
open_watchlist.meaning: Regulatory risk is now landing on the sector carrying the market, which raises the cost of a tech slip.
